description: This line plot illustrates the Accuracy@1 (%) for two large language models, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet, as a function of the number of child nodes in a tree search structure, labeled “Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width)” on the x-axis, which ranges from 1 to 7 with integer tick labels. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy@1 (%)”, spans from 15 to 35 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 5. The plot contains two lines: the GPT-4o line is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers, starting at 24.4% at a tree width of 1, rising to 28.9% at width 3, peaking at 34.4% at width 5, and then declining to 31.1% at width 7. The Claude-3.5-Sonnet line is represented by a dashed light purple line with star-shaped markers, starting at 26.7% at width 1, rising to 27.8% at width 3, declining to 24.4% at width 5, and further dropping to 20.0% at width 7.
caption_used: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (RIGHT) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with GPT-4o peaking at 31.1% and Claude-3.5-Sonnet consistently outperforming GPT-4o across all tree widths.
